successors.name: Kingdom of Saba
successors.text: the Jawf valley around Qarnawu (Ma'in) and Baraqish, Cliopatria's Minaean shape of 383-189 BCE: the Sabaeans regained control over Ma'in 'after the collapse of Qataban in 50 BC'

ledger.x: c. 625 BCE: Ma'in becomes a kingdom in the Jawf. 'transition from a city-state to kingdom in the last quarter of the 7th century BCE' (page); the city-state at Qarnawu is already in the record 'in the 8th century BCE'. -625 is the first year of that quarter, a reading of the page's span. The territory is not…
By -383 the north of the Jawf passes to Ma'in.
-188: Ma'in controls the incense road to the north.
-170: the Minaean reach extends to Dedan.
-50: the northern road leaves the state.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey exists for any Minaean frontier: the Jawf valley is approximate (pages name only towns), and the caravan road to Dedan is a line of stations, never a border.
